title: Witness protection scheme - does it work in practice
p1: A witness can know the truth behind a serious crime… but fear can stop them from speaking. This is where witness protection becomes a real test of the justice system.
p2: Many people think witness protection means simply giving someone a new identity. In reality, it is much broader. It can involve security, relocation, confidentiality, and other measures to ensure a witness can testify without intimidation.
p3: India introduced the Witness Protection Scheme to address a major challenge: witnesses often turn hostile because of threats, pressure, or fear. But the success of such protection depends on practical implementation, resources, and timely action. A strong law on paper is not enough if a witness still feels unsafe. The real measure is whether an ordinary person can trust the system enough to speak the truth.
conclusion: Do you think witness protection in India is strong enough to encourage people to come forward against powerful accused persons?
